evals.name: quiet-run-is-short-and-complete
evals.expected_output: Diffs the current detector output against the prior artifact, finds nothing moved, and says so briefly, with the window it covered and the suppressed count. It does not re-list standing findings, does not restate the previous run's candidate set, and does not pad the response to look useful. A delta run whose honest answer is 'nothing changed' is short and complete.
expectations: Reports 'nothing moved' briefly, with the window and the suppressed count
Does not re-list standing or previously reported findings
Does not pad a quiet run

evals.name: declined-findings-are-never-resurrected
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:delta — we declined the 'Testing conventions' move last week, has anything changed?
evals.expected_output: Reports movement without re-proposing the declined finding. A declined status is a decision, and a re-run does not reopen it — not as new, not as changed, and not 'for review'. If the declined section's source content changed, that is still not grounds to re-propose the same move; the response may note the content changed while leaving the decision standing. The reasoning is stated once: resurrecting decisions is how an operator learns to stop reading the report carefully.
expectations: Does not re-propose the declined finding in any shape
Leaves the declined status intact in the artifact
Explains why declined decisions are not reopened by a re-run

evals.name: broken-glob-is-the-cadence-justification
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:delta — nothing touched the rules folder this sprint.
evals.expected_output: Re-validates every previously-valid glob anyway and reports any that stopped resolving as broken-glob. It explains why the prompt's premise does not make the check unnecessary: a glob breaks when the code it described is renamed or moved, which is an ordinary refactor nowhere near the rules tree, produces no signal at the time, and leaves the rule silently not firing. That is the shape that most justifies running this on a cadence rather than only after editing rules.
expectations: Re-validates globs even when the rules tree is untouched
Reports a glob that stopped resolving as broken-glob
Explains that a refactor elsewhere breaks globs with no signal
Does not accept 'nothing touched the rules folder' as a reason to skip validation

evals.name: suppression-is-always-counted
evals.expected_output: Applies the noise budget to low-confidence, low-value new findings and reports the count of what it suppressed alongside the movement it is showing. The suppressed count is part of the report rather than an omission, because a delta that hides its own filtering is exactly the failure it was built to avoid — a report that reads as complete while covering a fraction.
expectations: Reports the suppressed count explicitly
Shows movement above the budget
States that hiding the filtering would defeat the skill's purpose

evals.name: no-prior-artifact-routes-out
evals.expected_output: Resolves the memory-tier home through the plugin's topic-docs binding, finds no stored baseline and no findings artifact, and says so plainly — then routes to the full audit as the skill that produces one. It does not silently run a full audit under the delta name: this skill reports movement, and with no baseline there is no movement to report. The distinction is stated rather than papered over, and nothing is written.
expectations: Resolves the home through the topic-docs binding rather than a machine-global key
Reports the absent baseline rather than treating it as an error
Routes to the full audit instead of silently becoming one
Writes nothing

evals.name: declined-finding-stays-declined-from-another-checkout
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:delta — running this from a second worktree of the same repo. Last week I declined IP-004 (the deploy-conventions section) from the main checkout.
evals.expected_output: Reads the placement baseline at the home the topic-docs binding resolves, finds IP-004 in its decisions table with status declined, and suppresses it — it is not reported as new, changed, or 'for review'. The baseline's path carries no branch segment and no checkout discriminator, so a decline recorded anywhere in this repository holds here; the run says which decisions it is honoring and counts them in the suppressed total. If the resolved memory root is the per-checkout default and this worktree has no baseline yet, it says that plainly rather than presenting the declined finding as new.
expectations: Suppresses the declined finding rather than re-proposing it
Attributes the suppression to the persisted baseline, not to ephemeral state
Counts the suppression in the reported total
States plainly when the resolved home holds no baseline instead of treating declines as absent
